key_insight: DuSS-PET reconstructs low-dose PET images without paired low- and full-dose training scans by enforcing consistency between images and image-derived pseudo-sinograms.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support lower-radiation PET imaging while reducing dependence on paired training scans, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: Uses a computational Noisier2Noise strategy with Bernoulli corruption to approximate low-count noise.
Combines an adaptive Swin transformer for pseudo-sinogram restoration with plug-and-play image enhancement.
Trains with self-supervised consistency constraints linking image and pseudo-sinogram representations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports multi-center, multi-dose evaluations showing improvements over other self-supervised methods, comparable or better results than fully supervised approaches, and generalization across scanner vendors.
watch_item: Pseudo-sinograms are image-derived approximations; the abstract provides no quantitative metrics or diagnostic-task validation.
paper_title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data
